messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: rstan and memory limitations
parts:
Hi,

Is it possible to run stan and then read the results directly from disk?  I have encounter memory problems for large panel data sets and large number of parameters. 
Basically I would like to rm(fit) before using extract and replace extract which reads parameters directly to the disk.
fit <- stan() # OK
traceplot(fit, pars = c(parst), inc_warmup = F) # OK
la <- extract(fit, permuted = TRUE) # FAILS
rm(fit)

Thanks for any insight,
Linas

messages.author: f53f4ca2c430170d
messages.subject: Re: rstan and memory limitations
parts: On Tuesday, September 1, 2015 at 7:42:59 AM UTC-4, Linas Mockus wrote:

Hi,

Is it possible to run stan and then read the results directly from disk?  I have encounter memory
problems for large panel data sets and large number of parameters.

In addition to the specific problem of not having enough memory there are a few long-standing issues with R/Rcpp/rstan and memory (I'm sure they'll get fixed someday but they're not straightforward).  For the moment I think the best practice for when you really need to save all those parameters is to use CmdStan to run the model, generate the giant .csv file by saving all the parameters, and then deal with processing a giant .csv file.  I think after the output refactor becomes part of the main branch it'll be easier to resolve these issues but until then... CmdStan is better than rstan at chugging its way through giant data sets.

Krzysztof

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: rstan and memory limitations
parts:
You can specify the sample_file argument to stan() to write the output to a .csv file. But there is no guarantee you will be able to successfully load it with read_stan_csv(). Cmdstan may work better because it does not save the warmup by default.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: rstan and memory limitations
parts:
On Tuesday, September 1, 2015 at 5:34:17 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Is the design intention not to have it be readable?

No, it is just slow and consumes a lot of memory due to

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/1321

so giant CSV files might not be readable with given hardware. If the CSV file is small enough relative to the hardware it works fine and has unit tests.

It is more likely to succeed with a giant CSV file if you do what Soga did

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-users/urZeEMjjPHM/R0S41-hQbPMJ

but then it will not come out as a stanfit object.

Ben
